title: ArrowUp after clicking the transcript bounces back to bottom before detaching
outcome:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-26 against HEAD 2769124 + the uncommitted scroll work   
  (498-line diff in SessionPaneView.scroll.ts, new session-pane-body-keyboard-
  ownership.ts). Supersedes the first write-up. Symptom (Greg): wheel to      
  bottom, click the transcript to take focus off the composer, press ArrowUp: 
  view moves up, snaps back down a few times, then finally scrolls. Greg      
  reports this has been 'fixed' repeatedly and keeps returning.               
                                                                              
  WHY IT KEEPS RETURNING. Every attempt so far (189fad7, 85892f1, 2769124, and
  the in-flight body-ownership hook) hardened the KEYDOWN INTENT layer: window
  capture, body-target acceptance, useSessionPaneBodyKeyboardOwnership, the   
  document bubble listener, resolveMessageStackKeyboardScrollIntent, the pre- 
  capture in markTailFollowDetachedByUser, movedUpAfterUserEscape. Each closed
  one more way the intent could be missed. None touched the SCROLL HANDLER,   
  which has no direction-aware fallback - so any remaining miss reproduces the
  identical bounce. The design is a single point of failure: detached         
  authority must be set by a keydown path BEFORE Blink's first animated scroll
  frame, or the handler re-attaches.                                          
                                                                              
  THE STRUCTURAL GAP (SessionPaneView.scroll.ts, handleMessageStackScroll     
  ~:1952-2029). Branch order: movedUpAfterUserEscape (needs detached authority
  already set) -> hasDetachedTailFollow && !isAtPhysicalBottom -> shouldStick 
  (bottom gap < SESSION_STICKY_BOTTOM_BAND_PX = 72 =>                         
  setTailFollowIntent(true), shouldStick:true) -> (hasDetached ||             
  movedUpFromRecordedPosition || !intent) -> else                             
  keepPaneScrollPositionPinned. movedUpFromRecordedPosition is consulted only 
  AFTER the sticky-band branch. One ArrowUp is a ~40px Blink line scroll,     
  inside the 72px band, so with intent still true the handler classifies the  
  upward move as 'still at bottom' and RE-ARMS tail-follow. From there any    
  repin trigger snaps the view back: repinAfterRelevantResize (:822;          
  activePageChanged forces a repin regardless of threshold, and scrolling up  
  MOUNTS virtualized pages, so each ArrowUp generates its own trigger),       
  handleBottomRepinRequest (:738), and the 1200ms                             
  isPaneProgrammaticBottomFollowActive branch (:1981) which force-writes      
  targetTop and returns early. Recovery: a second ArrowUp landing before the  
  next repin accumulates >72px, so the 4th branch finally detaches. That is   
  exactly 'up, back down a few times, then it works'.                         
                                                                              
  SECONDARY: the MAX_SAFE_INTEGER sentinel. Both movedUpFromRecordedPosition  
  (:1956) and movedUpAfterUserEscape (:1962) skip when previousTop is the     
  sentinel. The sentinel is written by scrollVirtualizedMessageStackToBottom  
  (:702 - used by scrollMessageStackToBoundary('bottom') and the settled      
  follow with preferVirtualizedBoundary, i.e. tab activation),                
  restorePinnedMessageStackBeforePaint (:2083), and the activity reattach     
  (:2376). In a pure wheel-to-bottom flow the recorded top is real (the       
  shouldStick branch writes node.scrollTop), so the sentinel is not the       
  primary cause, but after a tab switch / End / jump-to-latest / activity     
  reattach it blinds the escape branch and costs yet another keypress.        
                                                                              
  VERIFIED NOT THE CAUSE (do not re-hunt): the capture-phase history-demand   
  listeners (useInitialActiveTranscriptMessages.ts :304/:480) never           
  preventDefault or stopPropagation a body-target ArrowUp -                   
  isTranscriptDemandKeyEventInScope rejects a body-only composedPath;         
  conversation-markers only stops propagation on Escape; PaneTabs stops are   
  tab-local; the pane  root is not focusable so focus really lands on body;   
  the virtualizer DOES detach on the intent event (markUserScroll) - the pane 
  is the sole re-pinner. Also already landed in 2769124: scrollbar-gutter:    
  stable on .message-stack and the 2px idle resize hysteresis                 
  (SessionPaneView.resize-measurement.ts) - i.e. tm-vxbi F1/F2 are effectively
  done; cross-check and note there.                                           
                                                                              
  WHY TESTS PASS WHILE THE BUG PERSISTS: every regression exercises the       
  keydown path (SessionPaneView.scroll.test.ts :195-386, App.scroll-          
  behavior.test.tsx :1297-1317 dispatch keyDown on document.body and assert   
  the intent listener); the near-bottom-band tests (:2775, :2939) rely on a   
  mousedown/wheel intent firing first. No test starts attached-at-bottom and  
  feeds ONLY scroll frames (no keydown) followed by a repin trigger. A        
  fallback gap is invisible to that suite by construction.                    
                                                                              
  FIX - a direction-aware fallback in the scroll handler, layered UNDER the   
  existing intent paths (keep them; they give the frame-exact detach when they
  work):                                                                      
  F1. In handleMessageStackScroll, BEFORE the shouldStick branch, classify a  
  user-caused upward move: node.scrollTop decreased versus the recorded       
  position AND node.scrollHeight did not shrink since that record (a collapse 
  can legitimately clamp scrollTop downward, a growth never decreases it) AND 
  no programmatic follow owns the viewport (the                               
                                                                              
  === ROUND 2 (2026-08-27, after F1-F3 landed): STILL BOUNCES. Greg: 'scrolls 
  up, then snaps, a few times, before it scrolls.' Bundle verified fresh      
  (ui/dist 04:32 > scroll.ts 04:26; served from disk via ServeDir,            
  main.rs:117-133). Pane fallback is correct and hook-tests pass, but the     
  VIRTUALIZER is a co-owner of bottom authority and learns about detachment   
  only via (a) the normalized intent event (keydown path - the one that is    
  missed here) or (b) its own native-scroll classification.                   
                                                                              
  MECHANISM (virtualized-conversation-scroll-events.ts): isNativeUserMovement 
  (:57-70) requires |scrollHeight - lastNativeScrollHeight| < 1, and          
  lastNativeScrollHeightRef is updated ONLY on native scroll events (:234-    
  235). Any content change between the wheel-to-bottom frame and the ArrowUp  
  frame (deferred page mount, compaction, Mermaid remeasure) makes the first  
  upward frame look like a height change -> isNativeUserMovement=false ->     
  nativeScrollKeepsPassiveTailFollow (:72-93) returns TRUE because            
  tailFollowIntent is the liveTailPinned React prop                           
  (AgentSessionPanel.tsx:1212, one render behind the pane's ref) and there was
  no prior interaction -> shouldKeepBottomAfterLayoutRef=true (:295), no      
  detach, no lastUserScrollInputTime. Next commit (the page mount the upward  
  scroll itself causes): VirtualizedConversationMessageList.tsx :1867-1920    
  auto-scroll layout effect proceeds (keep-bottom true, not detached, no      
  cooldown, and hasUserScrollInteraction && !nearBottom is false INSIDE the   
  72px band) -> requestMessageStackBottomRepin -> pane refuses (its intent is 
  false) -> the virtualizer writes the bottom ITSELF via                      
  writeScrollTopAndSyncViewport(node, target, {intent:'bottom'}) (:1918-1920).
  That downward native frame reaches the pane handler at the physical bottom -
                                                                              
  | shouldStick branch -> RE-ATTACH. Repeats until scrollHeight is stable     
  | across two consecutive native events. The code comment at scroll-events   
  | :655-659 already names exactly this failure ('the pane and virtualizer    
  | disagree for one commit and a page measurement can snap the viewport      
  | downward').                                                               
                                                                              
  SECOND RESIDUAL (pane): the fallback sits BELOW                             
  isPaneProgrammaticBottomFollowActive() (:1981-1993), which force-reattaches 
  every frame for 1200ms after any bottom_follow write and is NOT cancelled by
  the fallback (the keydown path cancels it via                               
  takeMessageStackUserScrollAuthority). Idle starters: beforePaint repin      
                                                                              
  === ROUND 3 OBSERVATION (Greg, 2026-08-27, running UI): 'on ArrowUp it      
  scrolls a bit and jumps, a few times until it goes. Interestingly the scroll
  is SMOOTH (different from mouse wheel).' This is diagnostic, not incidental.
                                                                              
  THE ASYMMETRY. In this UI the message stack has no CSS scroll-behavior (the 
  only 'scroll-behavior: smooth' is .pane-tabs, styles.css:2784). Wheel is    
  APP-OWNED: the non-passive wheel listener preventDefaults and writes the    
  delta itself (SessionPaneView.scroll.ts:1373-1375 ->                        
  scrollMessageStackByDelta, scrollKind incremental) - one instant write per  
  event, hence 'not smooth', and every classifier sees a user-sourced         
  programmatic write. PageUp/PageDown are APP-OWNED deterministic writes with 
  scrollSource 'user' (scrollSessionMessageStackByPageJump). ArrowUp/ArrowDown
  are the ONLY navigation left to the browser: the pane publishes intent but  
  does not preventDefault, so Chrome runs its native smooth keyboard animation
  (Windows: ~40px over many compositor frames), and every one of those frames 
  is a NATIVE scroll event with no input prelude.                             
                                                                              
  WHY THAT BOUNCES. A multi-frame native animation gives both bottom-authority
  owners many chances to misclassify: the pane's 1200ms programmatic-follow   
  window force-reattaches any frame inside it; the virtualizer's              
  nativeScrollKeepsPassiveTailFollow treats a frame as passive whenever       
  scrollHeight changed since the last native event (page mount from the upward
  motion, card remeasure) while the tailFollowIntent React prop is still      
  stale-true. One misclassified frame -> a bottom restore write -> Chrome     
  cancels the native animation (programmatic scroll aborts the smooth-scroll  
  animator) -> the reader is back at the bottom -> the next ArrowUp starts the
  sequence again -> 'a few times until it goes'. Wheel can never bounce       
  because the app owns the write and there is exactly one frame per event.    
                                                                              
  NEXT STEP (per Greg via Codex seq 121): begin from a RUNNING-UI reproduction
  with instrumentation, not static review. Instrumentation plan (dev-only,    
  behind a query flag or localStorage key): a ring buffer                     
  window.__termalScrollTrace that records (a) every scrollTop write site with 
  scrollKind/scrollSource and the caller label (pane repin, pane fallback,    
  virtualizer restore, virtualizer page-height retry, settled follow), (b)    
  every native scroll frame with performance.now(), scrollTop, scrollH

=== NEXT STEP (Fable, 2026-08-27): running-UI trace without code changes. A read-only DevTools console snippet is at target/fable-verify/scroll-trace.js (gitignored). It wraps scrollTo and the scrollTop setter on every .message-stack (capturing a call stack per programmatic write), records every native scroll frame with scrollTop/scrollHeight/clientHeight/gap, listens to termal:message-stack-scroll-write / -user-scroll-intent / -bottom-repin-request with their detail, observes content-page resizes, and marks wheel/mousedown/Arrow keydowns with the active element. Procedure: paste into F12 console of the live UI -> wheel to bottom -> click a message card -> ONE ArrowUp -> wait 2s -> __termalScrollTrace.dump() (copies to clipboard) -> paste the dump into the bead or chat. The dump names the exact frame that snapped back and the writer (stack + event detail), which decides between the pane 1200ms window, the virtualizer restore, or another producer, and settles Option A vs B.
acceptance: On a virtualized session transcript attached at its physical bottom, after the reader presses the mouse on non-focusable message content so that keyboard focus leaves the composer for the message stack or for document.body, an ArrowUp keydown delivered to the focused element is handled by the app: its default is prevented, the message stack moves up by exactly one arrow step, and live tail-follow is detached in the same input task; both focus landings are covered.

After that ArrowUp, a change of the transcript's content height (a page mount or measurement) followed by a native scroll frame does not return the message stack to the bottom: its scrollTop stays at the post-key position and tail-follow stays detached; a second ArrowUp then moves it up by one more step, again without any return to the bottom.

Criteria 1 and 2 are asserted by an App-level Vitest regression added in the candidate, which passes, together with the existing ui/src/SessionPaneView.scroll*.test.ts* suites and ui/src/App.scroll-behavior.test.tsx, in a registered committed-input run on the candidate commit, and `npx tsc --noEmit` in ui/ is clean on that commit.
If the regression fails on master 995515bc, the candidate also contains the product fix that makes it pass, and no existing scroll test is weakened or removed.
